errors.description: The abstract attributes the in vivo benefit to CDCA or GW4064, but the described mouse groups received CDCA or INT-747; no GW4064-treated mouse group is specified. This misidentifies the intervention supporting the mouse findings.
errors.evidence: Abstract: “Treatment with the FXR agonist CDCA or GW4064 decreased body weight, renal lipid accumulation, as well as renal injury.” Methods list a HFD group with 0.1% CDCA and a 30 mg/kg INT-747 group; the mouse results likewise state treatment with “CDCA or INT-747.”

errors.description: The reported HFD exposure duration conflicts with the experimental timeline: mice entered the groups at 8 weeks of age and were euthanized after 12 weeks of treatment, yet the abstract says they were fed the HFD for 20 weeks. The described schedule supports 12 weeks of assigned diet before the 20-week-age endpoint.
errors.evidence: Methods: mice were purchased at 5 weeks, randomized “After 3 weeks,” and euthanized “After a 12-week treatment.” Abstract: “Mice were fed by a 60% kcal fat diet for 20 weeks.”

errors.location: Results, comparison of HFD-fed and control mice; Figure 5H caption
errors.description: Serum creatinine is reported with conflicting units, making the stated concentration uninterpretable without correction: the results use μmol/L, while the Figure 5H caption labels the same measurement mmol/L.
errors.evidence: Results: “serum creatinine (4.8 ± 1.3 vs. 1.11 μmol/L).” Figure 5H caption: “Serum Creatinine (mmol/L).”

errors.description: The specific claim that FXR disrupts the β-catenin/TCF4 complex is not directly supported by the described experiments. The manuscript reports FXR–β-catenin co-immunoprecipitation and TOPflash reporter activity, but describes no measurement of TCF4 or of β-catenin–TCF4 complex assembly. The reported results support an association and altered β-catenin-mediated transcription, while the asserted complex disruption remains a mechanistic concern.
errors.evidence: Abstract: “We showed that FXR could bind with β-catenin via the AF1 domain, and disrupt the assembly of the core β-catenin/TCF4 complex.” The co-immunoprecipitation methods/results describe detection of FXR and β-catenin; the reporter assay measures TOPflash activity. TCF4 is not included among the described assay targets.
